answer.evidence: The main body is the vanity cabinet. Its tan wood counter top fills rows 24-28, bounded by a dark back line at row 24 and a dark brown front-edge line at row 29 (#786048). Gray shadow starts at row 30. Below that, the front face runs rows 30-44 (15 rows) and shows two drawers and two doors with handles. The bottles and jars standing on the counter are decor. The mirror above (rows 1-22) is a tall vertical panel with a frame and no horizontal top surface, so I mark all_major_parts_have_top false, but the main cabinet body clearly shows a top and a front.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a white-framed mirror over a drawer counter with small bottles. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean toward the material tone, similar to the hedge and cheese-stall references, and it does not have the black-sticker look. Shading is shallower than the references. The white frame, the cabinet and the mirror glass each show only about 3-4 lightness steps, where Beodeul materials carry 5-6. The mirror pane and the cabinet fronts are broad, nearly uniform areas with a few glint or drawer-line accents and no grain or per-surface dotting. Measured density is 8 visible tones per tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Near-flat coverage is 16%, slightly above the cheese stall's 13% and well above the 0% of the hedge and well. Placed next to the stall and well it would read as flatter and thinner, so it falls just short of the bar.
